capabilities.title: Its own virtual machine
capabilities.plain: Each sandbox is a separate virtual machine (microVM or full VM), not a container sharing a kernel with neighbours.

capabilities.title: Root access
capabilities.plain: You (and the agent) can act as the administrator: install anything, change system settings.

capabilities.title: Docker inside
capabilities.plain: You can run Docker containers inside the sandbox.

capabilities.title: Nested virtualisation
capabilities.plain: You can start virtual machines inside the sandbox, for tools that need their own VM.

capabilities.title: Your own image
capabilities.plain: Start machines from your own Dockerfile or image instead of the provider's default.

capabilities.title: Any size you like
capabilities.plain: Choose CPU and memory freely instead of picking from a short list of fixed sizes.

capabilities.title: Large machines
capabilities.plain: Machines of 16 vCPU or 32 GiB memory or more are available.

capabilities.title: Resize while running
capabilities.plain: Change CPU or memory without stopping the machine or losing what is running.

capabilities.title: GPUs
capabilities.plain: Machines with a graphics processor, for running AI models or other GPU work inside the sandbox.

capabilities.title: Choose the region
capabilities.plain: You decide which part of the world the machine runs in.

capabilities.title: Runs in the EU
capabilities.plain: At least one region inside the European Union, for EU data rules.

capabilities.title: Pause keeps memory
capabilities.plain: Pausing keeps memory and running programs, so the machine resumes exactly where it was.

capabilities.title: Pre-started pools
capabilities.plain: Keep machines ready in advance so new work starts without waiting for a boot.

capabilities.title: Starts in under a second
capabilities.plain: The provider documents new or resumed machines being ready in under a second.

capabilities.title: Snapshots of files
capabilities.plain: Save the machine's files at a moment and restore them later.

capabilities.title: Snapshots with memory
capabilities.plain: A snapshot also keeps memory and running programs.

capabilities.title: Copy a running machine
capabilities.plain: Make copies of a machine while it keeps running.

capabilities.title: Pick an older snapshot
capabilities.plain: Restore any earlier snapshot, not only the latest one.

capabilities.title: Reusable templates
capabilities.plain: Turn a set-up machine into a template and start many new machines from it.

capabilities.title: Automatic backups
capabilities.plain: The provider takes backups for you on a schedule.

capabilities.title: Files survive a stop
capabilities.plain: Stopping the machine keeps its disk; starting it again finds the files where they were.

capabilities.title: Separate volumes
capabilities.plain: Storage that lives on after the machine is deleted and can be attached to a new one.

capabilities.title: One volume, several machines
capabilities.plain: Several machines can use the same storage at once.

capabilities.title: Mount outside storage
capabilities.plain: Attach an S3-style bucket or another outside filesystem as a folder.

capabilities.title: Large disk
capabilities.plain: Disks of 100 GiB or more are available.

capabilities.title: Can stay on indefinitely
capabilities.plain: A machine can run for weeks without being stopped for idleness or a session limit.

capabilities.title: Choose the idle timeout
capabilities.plain: You set how long an idle machine waits before it pauses or stops, including never.

capabilities.title: Wakes on a request
capabilities.plain: A paused machine starts again by itself when a web request or message arrives.

capabilities.title: Scheduled runs
capabilities.plain: Start a machine or a job on a schedule, like a cron job, without your own server.

capabilities.title: Public link to a port
capabilities.plain: A web address that reaches a program running in the sandbox.

capabilities.title: Private link
capabilities.plain: A link only you or people with a token or login can open.

capabilities.title: Real SSH
capabilities.plain: Connect with a standard SSH client from your own computer.

capabilities.title: Terminal in the browser
capabilities.plain: Open a command line on the machine from the provider's website.

capabilities.title: Tunnel to your computer
capabilities.plain: Reach a port inside the sandbox as if it were on your own machine (port forwarding).

capabilities.title: Non-web ports
capabilities.plain: Reach services that are not HTTP, such as a database or game server, over TCP.

capabilities.title: Your own domain
capabilities.plain: Serve what the machine runs at your own web address.

capabilities.title: Automatic HTTPS
capabilities.plain: The provider gets and renews the security certificate for your domain.

capabilities.title: Outbound data included
capabilities.plain: Data the machine sends out is free or comes with a published allowance.

capabilities.title: Allow only some sites
capabilities.plain: Limit which internet addresses the machine can reach.

capabilities.title: Turn the internet off
capabilities.plain: Run a machine with no internet access at all.

capabilities.title: Fixed outgoing IP
capabilities.plain: Traffic leaves from a known IP address that other services can whitelist.

capabilities.title: Stored secrets
capabilities.plain: Save API keys with the provider and have them appear in the machine as environment variables.

capabilities.title: Secrets the agent cannot read
capabilities.plain: Keys are added to outgoing requests by the provider, so the agent never sees them.

capabilities.title: Limited API keys
capabilities.plain: Create API keys that can do only some things, or only in one project.

capabilities.title: Create from the website
capabilities.plain: Start a machine by clicking in the provider's dashboard, with no terminal.

capabilities.title: Command-line tool
capabilities.plain: An official command-line tool.

capabilities.title: Python SDK
capabilities.plain: An official library for Python programs.

capabilities.title: TypeScript SDK
capabilities.plain: An official library for JavaScript or TypeScript programs.

capabilities.title: Documented HTTP API
capabilities.plain: A documented web API that any language can call.

capabilities.title: MCP server
capabilities.plain: An official MCP server, so an AI assistant can create and use sandboxes itself.

capabilities.title: Interactive terminal over the API
capabilities.plain: A program can open a live terminal session (PTY) in the sandbox, not just run one command.

capabilities.title: Files over the API
capabilities.plain: Read and write files in the sandbox through the SDK or API.

capabilities.title: Coding agents preinstalled
capabilities.plain: Claude Code, Codex or similar are already installed in the default image.

capabilities.title: Send it a prompt
capabilities.plain: The provider runs an agent for you: you send a prompt, it does the work in the sandbox.

capabilities.title: One-click Hermes
capabilities.plain: Hermes Agent can be set up without a terminal.

capabilities.title: One-click OpenClaw
capabilities.plain: OpenClaw can be set up without a terminal.

capabilities.title: Browser built in
capabilities.plain: A web browser (Chrome or Chromium) ready for an agent to drive.

capabilities.title: Desktop for computer use
capabilities.plain: A graphical desktop an agent can see and click, for computer-use agents.

capabilities.title: Runs other platforms' agents
capabilities.plain: Documented as the machine for Cursor cloud agents, Devin, Claude Managed Agents or similar.

capabilities.title: Team workspace
capabilities.plain: Several people share machines, billing and keys.

capabilities.title: Roles and permissions
capabilities.plain: Give people different powers, such as read-only or admin.

capabilities.title: Single sign-on
capabilities.plain: Log in through your company's identity provider (SAML or OIDC).

capabilities.title: Hard spending cap
capabilities.plain: Set a limit the bill cannot go over; machines stop instead.

capabilities.title: Usage alerts
capabilities.plain: Get told when spending passes an amount you set.

capabilities.title: Audit log
capabilities.plain: A record of who did what in the account.

capabilities.title: Billed per second
capabilities.plain: Usage is counted to the second rather than by the hour or month.

capabilities.title: CPU billed only while working
capabilities.plain: An idle processor costs nothing or very little.

capabilities.title: Paused costs only storage
capabilities.plain: A paused or stopped machine bills for its kept files only, not CPU or memory.

capabilities.title: No monthly fee
capabilities.plain: Pay only for what you use, with no plan fee.

capabilities.title: Flat monthly price
capabilities.plain: A fixed price per month for a machine, so the bill is predictable.

capabilities.title: Ongoing free tier
capabilities.plain: Something keeps working for free every month, not only at the start.

capabilities.title: Free starting credit
capabilities.plain: Credit to spend when you sign up.

capabilities.title: Try without a card
capabilities.plain: You can start without entering a payment card.

capabilities.title: Public status page
capabilities.plain: A page showing outages and incidents.

capabilities.title: Uptime promise (SLA)
capabilities.plain: A written promise about availability, usually with credits if broken.

capabilities.title: SOC 2 report
capabilities.plain: An independent security audit report you can request.

capabilities.title: Data processing agreement
capabilities.plain: A GDPR data processing agreement is offered.

capabilities.title: Open source or self-hostable
capabilities.plain: The sandbox software can be run on your own servers.
